verbalization: Thioguanine is linked to the Prostaglandin E2 receptor EP4 subtype through a complex biological pathway. The evidence suggests that thioguanine acts as a target of SK-HEP1, a cell line that is specifically targeted by thioguanine. This targeting relationship is supported by the presence of a specific compound, [(1R,2R,3S,8R,10R,11S,12R,14R,16S,17R,18R,19R)-3-acetyloxy-16-(furan-3-yl)-18,19-dihydroxy-2,7,7,11,17-pentamethyl-5-oxo-6,13-dioxapentacyclo[9.8.0.02,8.012,14.012,17]nonadecan-10-yl] acetate, which is identified as the target of SK-HEP1. This compound is directly associated with the Prostaglandin E2 receptor EP4 subtype, indicating a potential mechanism by which thioguanine may influence this receptor. The integration of these findings suggests that thioguanine may exert its effects through interactions with the EP4 receptor, possibly modulating signaling pathways involving prostaglandin E2. The evidence highlights a direct and specific relationship between thioguanine and the EP4 receptor, supported by the presence of a specific compound that mediates this interaction.
